title: Circulating miRNA Signatures in Preeclampsia: Potential Biomarkers for Differentiating Preeclampsia from Gestational Hypertension
content: Background and Objectives: Preeclampsia (PE) and gestational arterial hypertension (GAH) are major hypertensive disorders of pregnancy with overlapping clinical manifestations, which may complicate their differential diagnosis. Circulating microRNAs (miRNAs) are emerging as potential minimally invasive biomarkers reflecting placental dysfunction, hypoxia, impaired trophoblast invasion, angiogenic imbalance, and endothelial dysfunction. This study aimed to evaluate the expression profile of circulating miRNAs in women with PE and GAH and to identify candidate molecular markers capable of differentiating these conditions. Materials and Methods: A case-control study included 101 pregnant women: 39 women with physiologic pregnancy (control group), 23 women with GAH, and 39 women with PE. Plasma levels of 15 candidate miRNAs were quantified using TaqMan-based quantitative reverse-transcription PCR. Results: Twelve of the 15 investigated miRNAs demonstrated significant differences between PE and the control group and between PE and GAH after multiple-testing correction. The most pronounced decrease in PE was observed for miR-210-3p, with a log2 fold-change of −2.06 versus controls and −2.12 versus GAH. In ROC analysis, miR-210-3p showed the highest discriminatory performance for both comparisons, with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.830 (95% CI, 0.735–0.925) for PE versus controls and 0.823 (95% CI, 0.720–0.925) for PE versus GAH. Other miRNAs, including miR-144-3p, miR-363-3p, miR-29a-3p, and miR-16-5p, also demonstrated moderate-to-good discriminatory performance. Conclusions: PE is characterized by a distinct circulating miRNA profile that differs from both physiologic pregnancy and GAH, whereas the molecular profile of GAH was broadly comparable to that of controls. Among the investigated candidates, miR-210-3p demonstrated the most consistent discriminatory performance and may represent a promising biomarker candidate for differentiating PE from GAH. A combination of several miRNAs may provide greater diagnostic value than individual markers.
